prompt: Some people think It's better to choose friends who always hav the same opinions as them. Other people believe it is good to have friends who sometimes disagree with them Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Some people believe that it is preferable to have friends who share similar views and interests, while others argue that friendships are more beneficial when people are willing to disagree with one another. Although having things in common can make it easier to form a friendship, I believe that occasional disagreement is equally valuable because it allows friends to give honest advice and develop greater trust.

On the one hand, sharing similar interests and perspectives can make it considerably easier for people to establish friendships. When individuals enjoy the same activities or have similar ways of thinking, they have more topics to discuss and are likely to feel comfortable in each other's company. As a result, they may spend more time together, allowing familiarity and trust to develop naturally. For example, two university students who both enjoy playing basketball may regularly meet after classes to practise or watch games together. Their shared interest gives them a natural reason to interact, which can gradually develop into a close friendship.

On the other hand, having a friend who is willing to disagree can be particularly valuable because genuine friends do not simply tell each other what they want to hear. Instead, they can point out weaknesses in each other's decisions and provide advice based on their honest opinions. This can help individuals avoid poor decisions while also creating a stronger sense of trust, since they know that their friends are being sincere rather than merely trying to please them. For instance, someone choosing an outfit for an important occasion may ask a close friend for advice precisely because they expect an honest response. Even if the friend recommends a different outfit, this constructive disagreement may be more useful than automatic approval and can reinforce the trust between them.

In conclusion, similar interests and perspectives can provide a strong foundation for forming friendships because they encourage comfortable and frequent interaction. Nevertheless, I believe that the ability to disagree honestly is also essential, as sincere advice can help friends make better decisions and build deeper trust.
